title: Well-posedness: exhibit uniform lattices in real semisimple groups with $2$-torsion

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Confirm the hypothesis is non-vacuous and characterize the class addressed.

**Obligation.** Cite/exhibit uniform (cocompact) lattices $\Gamma$ in real semisimple Lie groups containing $2$-torsion (e.g. arithmetic cocompact lattices with finite-order elements, or reflection-type lattices). State explicitly that such $\Gamma$ have finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups (cocompactness) so the local-replacement program over singular strata is finite in type.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolved.** Added a *Well-posedness* subsection (\S\ref{sec:wellposed}) at the head of the Standing-data section, with two propositions.

**Prop. (Existence of uniform lattices with 2-torsion)** exhibits concrete examples in real semisimple groups:
- (E1) Hyperbolic Coxeter/reflection lattices $W(P)\le O(n,1)^+$ for compact Coxeter polytopes $P\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ (Poincare polyhedron thm; Lanner small-$n$ simplices, right-angled 120-cell for $n=4$, Bugaenko compact examples up to $n=8$). Facet reflections are order-2; 2-torsion persists in $SO(n,1)^+$ via $\pi$-rotations about codim-2 faces.
- (E2) Arithmetic cocompact lattices $\mathrm{O}(f,\mathcal{O}_k)$ from $k$-anisotropic quadratic forms of signature $(n,1)$ at one real place and definite at all others (explicit: $x_0^2+\dots+x_{n-1}^2-\sqrt2\,x_n^2$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$). Cocompactness via Godement/Borel-Harish-Chandra (anisotropy => no unipotents/$\mathbb{Q}$-split torus); $-\mathrm{Id}$ and coordinate reflections give involutions. Noted analogues in $SU(n,1)$ and $SL_2$-type groups via hermitian/quaternionic forms.

This shows the hypothesis of Problem 7 is **non-vacuous** in arbitrarily large dimension.

**Prop. (Finiteness of the local data)** proves, for any uniform lattice acting properly cocompactly on $X=G/K$:
- (F1) every finite subgroup fixes a point (Cartan fixed-point thm on the CAT(0) space $X$ / containment in a maximal compact), so isotropy groups are finite;
- (F2) finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, via the standard cocompact-properness count ($\#\{\gamma:\gamma C\cap C\neq\emptyset\}<\infty$ for compact $C$ with $\Gamma C=X$).

Hence the local-replacement program runs over **finitely many distinct isotropy types** $(F,\rho_F)$ -- it is *finite in type* -- and $F=\mathbb{Z}/2$ is always among them when $\Gamma$ has 2-torsion (handled unconditionally in \S\ref{sec:Z2}); the global resolution then grafts one model per type, which is why it terminates.

The global section's Lemma already invoked finiteness of stabilizer conjugacy classes; this new subsection now states/proves it explicitly and supplies the requested concrete witnesses. Brace/environment balance verified; no LaTeX toolchain available locally to compile.
